intro: Can StreamMUSE's real-time rap get a better lyric writer and a better voice without losing real time? Part 1 compares lyric models on the same 15 prompts. Part 2 compares text-to-speech models on the same 20 two-bar lines, cloned from the same reference voice and warped onto the beat exactly as the live system does. Part 3 runs the full live system (protocol v3: lyric stream plus per-bar synthesis) with the most promising combinations, at 90 BPM (96 bars, eight live edits) and 120 BPM (48 bars, four edits). The resulting v1.1 is Qwen3.5-9B for lyrics and MOSS-TTS-Local v1.5 with continuation for the voice, both on one GPU.
llm: Each model wrote all 16 bars of the 15 demo-page prompts (240 bars) with v1.0's writer: 32 candidates per bar, couplet rhymes, syllable and stress checks, rescue waves. First-wave pass is the share of the 32 candidates that pass the checks; the syllable count rejects most of the rest for every model. Times are on one H200 with the lyric model alone. The two hyphen rows tried asking for syllables split with hyphens; both got worse and were dropped.
tts: Each voice spoke the 20 two-bar corpus lines twice (40 pairs), one bar per request as in v1.0, cloned from the reference below. Every take went through the same MMS alignment and Rubber Band R3 warp onto the beat; the players here are those warped vocals, without drums. Quality scores: Whisper word error rate, speaker similarity between the two bars and to the reference (ECAPA), and the loudness and pitch jump across the bar line. Times are per bar on an otherwise idle H200, one request at a time.
sessions: Full live sessions from the Mac over the tunnel to the H200, each stack started fresh. Latest/Older/eSpeak count the bars by the voice actually played; older means an edit came too late for that bar and its earlier version played. Startup wait is the time from pressing start to the first sound. Audio lead is how long before its bar the server audio reached the Mac. Qwen3.8-27B slows the voice when it shares the GPU, and the GPU 2 rows put it next to another user's training job, which starved it of lyrics.
method: Hardware: one NVIDIA H200 (GPU 1) for everything unless a row says GPU 2. GPU 2 was running another user's training job at 90 to 100% utilization the whole time, so it only hosted the quality runs of the voices (whose times are not reported) and the 'GPU 2' session rows. A Qwen3-8B server from another project shared GPU 1 but stayed idle.

Lyric models were served by vLLM 0.24 with thinking disabled (chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false), FP8 checkpoints for the 27B and 35B models, at most 2048 tokens per request. The Qwen3.5 and later models are hybrid-attention models; vLLM recomputes the shared prompt for each of the 32 candidates (no prefix cache hits), which is why the 27B models need about 0.9 s per bar.

Voices: MOSS-TTS v1.5 on SGLang-Omni 0.1.4 with StreamMUSE's latency and continuation patches (v1.0's voice); MOSS-TTS-Local v1.5, Higgs TTS 3, Fish Audio S2 Pro and Qwen3-TTS 1.7B on SGLang-Omni 0.1.8 with default configurations; IndexTTS-2.5 through its own Python API (no serving optimizations, so its time is not comparable). Continuation for MOSS-TTS-Local was ported to 0.1.8 (patches/sglang-omni-0.1.8-moss-local-continuation.patch). Voxtral TTS was excluded (its open weights cannot clone a voice) and Fish Audio Drama 3 is not supported by SGLang-Omni 0.1.8.
Durations: MOSS models are asked for the bar's length (token count) and hit it; the others speak at their own pace and the R3 warp fits them.

Sessions use the v1.0 client unchanged; the server adds --vllm-extra-payload (for thinking off) and --moss-sglang-resample-output (MOSS-TTS-Local returns 48 kHz stereo). All audio here is loudness-normalized to -16 LUFS MP3 at 192 kbps.
